Author: Virender Singh Bench: Virender Singh IN THE HIGH COURT OF HIMACHAL PRADESH AT SHIMLA Cr. MP(M) No. 2793 of 2023 Reserved on : 7.11.2023 Decided on : 17.11.2023 Rohit Kumar ... Applicant Versus State of H.P.

R e s p o n d e n t _____________________________________________________________ Coram Hon'ble Mr. Justice Virender Singh, Judge Whether approved for reporting?

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF HIMACHAL PRADESH AT SHIMLA
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: _ _ ______ For the Applicant : Mr. Shyam Singh Chauhan, Advocate.

For the Respondent : Mr. Tejasvi Sharma, Addl. A.G. with Ms. Leena Guleria, Dy. A.G., assisted by ASI Om Prakash, I.O.
Police Station, Paonta Sahib, Sirmour, H.P. Virender Singh, Judge Applicant- Rohit Kumar has filed the present application, under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.'), for releasing him on bail, during the pendency of trial, in case FIR No. 07/2023,
dated 8.1.2023, registered with Police Station, Paonta Sahib, District Sirmour, H.P., under Sections 366 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'the IPC").
2. According to the applicant, he is an innocent person and has falsely been implicated, in this case.
3. According to the applicant, he is having no criminal antecedents and has deep roots in the society.
4. The applicant, through his counsel, has given certain undertakings, for which he is ready to abide by, in case, ordered to be released on bail.
5.
On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the present application.

6. When put to notice, the Police filed the status report, disclosing therein that on 8.1.2023, the father of the prosecutrix appeared before the Police, disclosing therein that he is resident of the address, mentioned in the application and his daughter (child victim), whose age has been mentioned in the complaint as 16 years, had been enticed away by Rohit Kumar (applicant).
6.1 The complainant had searched for his daughter.
According to him, the applicant, aged about 25 years, had enticed away his daughter.
He has apprehended that the applicant could commit crime against his daughter and kill her.
6.2 On the basis of above facts, the Police registered a case against the applicant and criminal machinery swung into motion.

entities.text: Rohit Kumar vs State Of H.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During investigation, the complainant produced the photo copy of the birth certificate of the child victim, according to which, her date of birth is 1.1.2008.
On 8.1.2023, the child victim telephonically informed her father, disclosing that she is coming from Delhi to Dehradun.
The child victim was found at Bus Stand, Dehradun.
She was sent for medico-legal examination at Civil Hospital, Paonta Sahib.

6.4 On the basis of statement of child victim, recorded under Section 161 Cr. P.C., provisions of Section 376 of the IPC, read with Section 4 of Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the POCSO Act') were added in this case.

entities.text: Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The child victim was produced before the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Paonta Sahib, District Sirmour,
where her statement under Section 164 of Cr. P.C. was recorded.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Paonta Sahib
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6.5 As per the statement of child victim, accused has committed rape upon her.
On 12.1.2023, the accused was arrested.
He was also medico legally examined.

The physical evidence, so collected,
during medico legal examination of the child victim, as well as, of the applicant, were sent for SFSL,
Junga and the result of the same has been received.
6.6 During investigation, it was found that the document, pertaining to the birth of child victim, which was produced by the complainant, was not found to be genuine.
6.7 The parents of the child victim could not produce any document, with regard to date of birth of the child victim.
As such, the child victim was sent for ossification test, according to which, the age of the child victim was found to be more than 18 years.
As such, the Police has deleted the provisions of Section 363 IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act.
However, Section 365 of the IPC has been added, in this case.

6.8 After completion of investigation, Police has submitted report, under Section 173 (2) Cr. P.C., for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 365 and 376 of the IPC, before the Court of learned Special Judge (Rape & POCSO), Sirmour at Nahan (hereinafter referred to as 'the trial Court').

entities.text: Special Judge (Rape & POCSO), Sirmour at Nahan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The case is now stated to be fixed for 29.12.2023.
7.
On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.
8. In the status report, no criminal history of the applicant has been mentioned nor the same has been argued by the learned Additional Advocate General, during the course of the arguments.

9. Initially, the Police has added the provisions of Section 363 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act,
but as per the stand taken by the Police, in the status report, later on, both these sections were deleted and provisions of Section 365 of the IPC have been added, in this case.
10. The applicant cannot be kept in judicial custody, for indefinite period, as the chances of commencement and conclusion of trial, against the applicant, are not so bright.
11. The role, allegedly played by the applicant, will be proved during the course of the trial.

The application cannot be dismissed, as a matter of punishment, as, pre-trial punishment is prohibited Rohit Kumar vs State Of H.P on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67507968/
2 under the law.

entities.text: Rohit Kumar vs State Of H.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. The applicant being resident of Uttar Pradesh does not mean that his bail application cannot be allowed.
Considering the said fact, stringent conditions can be imposed, upon him, in case the application is allowed.

13. It is no longer res-integra that at the time of deciding the bail-application, detailed discussion about the evidence, so collected by the prosecution, during the investigation, should be avoided, as it would cause prejudice to the case of the applicant, as well as, the prosecution.
14. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be allowed and is accordingly allowed.

15. The applicant is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No. 7 of 2023, dated 8.1.2023,
registered with Police Station, Paonta Sahib, District Sirmour, under Sections 366 and 376 of the IPC, on his furnishing personal bail bond, in the sum of 50,000/-, with two sureties, in the like amount, out of which, one surety should be local, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court.

entities.text: Police Station, Paonta Sahib, District Sirmour
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 16. Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall not be taken as an expression of opinion, on the merits of the case, as these observations, are confined, only, to the disposal of the present bail application.
17. It is made clear that the respondent-State is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions, is found to be violated by the applicant.

18. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of Model Central Jail, Nahan, through email, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the e-prison software.

Rohit Kumar vs State Of H.P on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67507968/
3 19.

sentences.text:
In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of Model Central Jail, Nahan, is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary,
DLSA, Nahan.

The Superintendent of Model Central Jail, Nahan, is further directed that if the applicant fails to furnish the bail bonds, as per the order passed by this Court, within a period of one month from today, then, the said fact be submitted to this Court.

(Virender Singh) Judge November 17, 2023 Kalpana Rohit Kumar vs State Of H.P on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67507968/
